:::{#def-local-maximizer}
#### Local maximizer

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$.
A point $\vx^* \in \reals^p$ is a **local maximizer** of $f$
if there is a number $\tolin > 0$
such that $f(\vx^*) \ge f(\vx)$
for all $\vx \in \reals^p$ with $\norm{\vx - \vx^*} < \tolin$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-local-maximizer}
#### A local maximizer

Let $f(x) = 1 - x^2$.
For every $x \in \reals$,

$$
\ba
f(0) - f(x)
&= 1 - (1 - x^2)
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= x^2
&& \text{(simplify)}
\\
&\ge 0,
&& \text{(a square)}
\ea
$$

so $f(0) \ge f(x)$ for all $x$, and $0$ is a local maximizer of $f$ with any $\tolin > 0$.

:::
